sources.note: Nothing on Kontanawa stress. Kontanawa appears only in Table 2 section III (p.15): 'Other ethnonyms said to designate Panoan languages/dialects but with no further clues as to their classification' — 'Kontanawa (Tastevin, 1929: 13; Aguiar, 2007: 40, 48)'; ethnonym index p.81 'Kontanawa (T2: III) – var: Contanawa, Kontanua, Kuntanawa'; location appendix p.111 (upper Tarauacá, between upper Envira and Muru, citing Tastevin 1919: 146; 1925: 415; 1926: 34, 49). Fleck's phonology/stress discussion concerns attested Panoan languages only.

sources.citation: Instituto Socioambiental, Povos Indígenas no Brasil: 'Kuntanawa' (entry by Mariana Ciavatta Pantoja, publ. 01/2009, rev. 2021), section 'Língua e situação sociolingüística'.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; states the language is no longer spoken: 'Os Kuntanawa, povo da família lingüística Pano, não falam mais sua língua indígena. Todos falam o português. Esforços de reconstrução da língua têm sido realizados por meio de fragmentos ainda vivos na memória da matriarca do grupo, dona Mariana, do contato com outros povos de língua Pano (como os Kaxinawa e os Yawanawa) e da grafia que utilizam, e de canções ayahuasqueiras.' Bibliography is ethnographic (Pantoja 2008 Os Milton; Tastevin 1925, 1926; Aquino & Iglesias 1994; Macedo 1988).

sources.citation: Tastevin, Constant. 1919. Quelques considérations sur les Indiens du Juruá. Bulletins et Mémoires de la Société d'Anthropologie de Paris VI:10, 144-154. DOI 10.3406/bmsap.1919.8875.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No linguistic data on Kontanawa: p.146 lists 'les Kontanauas' among the Juruá tribes and places them on the Haut-Tarauacá; p.152 lists 'les Kontanawas' among the tribes whose name ends in -nawa. The only accent remark is a general one about the ethnonym element nawa, not this language: 'l'accent tonique du mot nâwa se trouve sur la pénultième, et qu'on prononce plus souvent naw que nâwa' (p.153). (Persée docAsPDF is altcha-blocked; per-page scanned text downloaded instead.)

sources.citation: Hammarström, Forkel, Haspelmath & Bank. Glottolog 5.3, languoid kont1246 'Kontanáwa' (Unattested; Ethnologue-comment on attestation).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Says the language is unattested: 'no linguistic data has been published to contradict or verify that Kontanáwa is a different language (as opposed to merely a dialect of a different ethnic group, or a different ethnic group who no longer speak their ancestral language) from other Nawa-languages'. Only two refs, both 'a wordlist or less': Aguiar 2007 (overview/socling) and Tastevin 1919 (ethnographic overview).

sources.note: Wikipedia: 'Kontanáwa (Kuntanawa), was rediscovered in 1987, reported bilingual in their language and Portuguese. However, no linguistic information is available, and it is not known if they speak a distinct language.' Catalog searches returned no linguistic work: OpenAlex 0, CrossRef 1 (Pantoja & Meyer 2014, ethnographic), Semantic Scholar 0, BDTD 0, oasisbr 1 (ayahuasca anthropology). DuckDuckGo/Bing/Mojeek/Marginalia by automated download were blocked or empty.
